# PathPricer — Full Quantitative Specification & Architecture Guide

> An interactive European option pricing platform that benchmarks Monte Carlo simulation techniques against analytical Black-Scholes prices, fits Heston stochastic-volatility and SVI volatility-surface models, and evaluates model-aware delta-hedging strategies.

- Website: https://pathpricer.vercel.app
- Codebase: https://github.com/karbburn/PathPricer
- Social & OG Image: https://pathpricer.vercel.app/pathpricer.png

---

## 1. Mathematical Framework & Pricing Engine

### 1.1 Geometric Brownian Motion (GBM)
The underlying asset follows:
$$dS_t = (r - q) S_t dt + \sigma S_t dW_t$$

Exact terminal price simulation under the risk-neutral measure:
$$S_T = S_0 \exp\left( \left(r - q - \frac{1}{2}\sigma^2\right)T + \sigma \sqrt{T} Z \right), \quad Z \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$$

### 1.2 Black-Scholes-Merton Closed-Form Benchmark
For a European Call ($C$) and Put ($P$):
$$d_1 = \frac{\ln(S_0 / K) + (r - q + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^2)T}{\sigma\sqrt{T}}$$
$$d_2 = d_1 - \sigma\sqrt{T}$$

$$C = S_0 e^{-qT} N(d_1) - K e^{-rT} N(d_2)$$
$$P = K e^{-rT} N(-d_2) - S_0 e^{-qT} N(-d_1)$$

#### Analytical Greeks
- **Delta ($\Delta$)**:
  - Call: $e^{-qT} N(d_1)$
  - Put: $-e^{-qT} N(-d_1)$
- **Gamma ($\Gamma$)**:
  - Both: $\frac{e^{-qT} N'(d_1)}{S_0 \sigma \sqrt{T}}$
- **Vega ($\mathcal{V}$)**:
  - Both: $S_0 e^{-qT} \sqrt{T} N'(d_1)$
- **Theta ($\Theta$)**:
  - Call: $-\frac{S_0 \sigma e^{-qT} N'(d_1)}{2\sqrt{T}} - r K e^{-rT} N(d_2) + q S_0 e^{-qT} N(d_1)$
  - Put: $-\frac{S_0 \sigma e^{-qT} N'(d_1)}{2\sqrt{T}} + r K e^{-rT} N(-d_2) - q S_0 e^{-qT} N(-d_1)$
- **Rho ($\rho$)**:
  - Call: $K T e^{-rT} N(d_2)$
  - Put: $-K T e^{-rT} N(-d_2)$

---

## 2. Monte Carlo Estimators & Variance Reduction

### 2.1 Standard Monte Carlo
Draw $N$ independent Gaussian samples $Z_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$:
$$\hat{V}_{\text{MC}} = e^{-rT} \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N f(S_T^{(i)})$$
Standard error: $\text{SE} = \frac{s}{\sqrt{N}}$, achieving $\mathcal{O}(N^{-1/2})$ convergence.

### 2.2 Antithetic Variates
Pairs $Z_i$ with $-Z_i$:
$$\hat{V}_{\text{anti}} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N/2} \frac{f(S_T(Z_i)) + f(S_T(-Z_i))}{2}$$
Since option payoff is monotone with respect to $Z$, $\text{Cov}(f(Z), f(-Z)) < 0$, typically cutting variance by 40–60%.

### 2.3 Control Variates
Uses the terminal asset price $S_T$ whose risk-neutral expectation is known exactly: $\mathbb{E}[S_T] = S_0 e^{(r-q)T}$.
$$\hat{V}_{\text{CV}} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N \left( f(S_T^{(i)}) - \beta^* \left( S_T^{(i)} - S_0 e^{(r-q)T} \right) \right)$$
Where optimal weight is:
$$\beta^* = \frac{\widehat{\text{Cov}}(f(S_T), S_T)}{\widehat{\text{Var}}(S_T)}$$

### 2.4 Combined Antithetic + Control Variates
Applies control variate regression to the pairwise antithetic averaged payoffs, yielding the highest statistical efficiency and lowest standard error.

### 2.5 Randomized Quasi-Monte Carlo (RQMC)
Generates low-discrepancy Sobol sequence points scrambled using Owen randomization across $M=20$ independent replications. Integrates smoothly to achieve convergence rates approaching $\mathcal{O}(N^{-1})$.

---

## 3. Implied Volatility Solver
Finds $\sigma$ such that:
$$\text{BS}_{\text{price}}(S_0, K, T, r, q, \sigma, \text{type}) - P_{\text{market}} = 0$$

- **Initialization**: Brenner-Subrahmanyam approximation: $\sigma_0 \approx \sqrt{\frac{2\pi}{T}} \frac{P_{\text{market}}}{S_0}$
- **Primary algorithm**: Newton-Raphson iterations using exact analytical Vega: $\sigma_{n+1} = \sigma_n - \frac{f(\sigma_n)}{\mathcal{V}(\sigma_n)}$
- **Fallback**: Brent's bounded bracket method when Vega approaches 0 (deep in/out-of-the-money or near expiry).

---

## 4. P&L Attribution ("P&L Explain")
Decomposes actual repriced option portfolio value change $\Delta P$ using Taylor series expansion:
$$\Delta P \approx \Delta \cdot \Delta S + \frac{1}{2}\Gamma (\Delta S)^2 + \mathcal{V} \cdot \Delta \sigma + \Theta \cdot \Delta t + \rho \cdot \Delta r + \varepsilon$$
- $\Delta \cdot \Delta S$: First-order spot directional impact
- $\frac{1}{2}\Gamma (\Delta S)^2$: Spot convexity (Gamma profit/loss)
- $\mathcal{V} \cdot \Delta\sigma$: Volatility sensitivity
- $\Theta \cdot \Delta t$: Deterministic time decay
- $\rho \cdot \Delta r$: Interest rate shift impact
- $\varepsilon$: Cross-Greeks residual (Vanna, Volga, higher-order non-linearities)

---

## 5. Advanced Volatility Modeling

### 5.1 Heston Stochastic Volatility Model
$$dS_t = (r - q)S_t dt + \sqrt{V_t} S_t dW_t^S$$
$$dV_t = \kappa (\theta - V_t) dt + \xi \sqrt{V_t} dW_t^V$$
$$\mathbb{E}[dW_t^S dW_t^V] = \rho dt$$

Priced analytically via Carr-Madan Fourier transform inversion:
- Calibrated to market chains via Differential Evolution followed by L-BFGS-B gradient polishing.
- Enforces Feller condition check: $2\kappa\theta > \xi^2$.

### 5.2 SVI (Stochastic Volatility Inspired) Surface
Total implied variance $w(k) = \sigma^2(k) T$ parameterized by log-moneyness $k = \ln(K/F)$:
$$w(k) = a + b \left( \rho (k - m) + \sqrt{(k - m)^2 + \sigma^2} \right)$$
Slice-by-slice calibration with butterfly arbitrage verification via the Durrleman condition.

### 5.3 Delta-Hedging Simulation Benchmark
Simulates continuous-time underlying paths under stochastic volatility, executing discrete delta hedging at fixed rebalancing frequencies:
- Compares naive Black-Scholes delta hedging (fixed IV) vs model-aware Heston delta hedging.
- Quantifies tracking error variance and hedging variance reduction ratio.

---

## 6. Web Application Architecture

- **Frontend**: Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, KaTeX.
- **Backend API**: FastAPI (Python 3.12), NumPy (vectorized array operations), SciPy (root finding and optimization).
- **SEO & Social**: OpenGraph image (`/pathpricer.png`, 1728x910), Twitter Card summary_large_image, Web App Manifest, Schema.org JSON-LD (SoftwareApplication, WebSite).
- **Deployment**: Vercel (Frontend), Render (Compute Engine).
